en.h1: Iguazu Falls and the Devil's Throat: what to see in Puerto Iguazu
en.title: Puerto Iguazu Travel Guide | What to See, Best Places & Tips
content_excerpts: Puerto Iguazú undoubtedly secured its place on the global tourist map thanks to the breathtaking Iguazú Falls. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984, these majestic falls can be admired from both the Argentine and Brazilian sides. While Puerto Iguazú is smaller and more tranquil compared to its Brazilian neighbor, Foz do Iguaçu, it offers equally close access to the stunning waterfalls.

Rising higher than Niagara Falls and stretching twice as wide with 275 cascades arranged in a dramatic horseshoe over nearly two miles of the Iguaçu River, the Iguazú Falls are a striking natural wonder formed by a volcanic eruption that created a massive fissure in the earth. A visit to these falls offers a truly awe-inspiring experience, where the sheer power and thunderous roar of the cascades leave an indelible impression. Alongside Nahuel Huapi National Park in Patagonia, Iguazú Falls ranks as one of Argentina's most popular tourist destinations. Visitors are treated to breathtaking views, with opportunities for guided tours, trekking, and water sports at the base of this majestic site.

en.h1: Train to the Clouds and Seven Colors Mountain: what to see in Salta
en.title: Salta Travel Guide | What to See, Best Places & Tips
content_excerpts: The Province of Salta is situated in the Northwest of Argentina and it borders three countries: Chile, Bolivia and Paraguay, besides of six Argentinian provinces: Jujuy , Formosa , Chaco, Santiago del Estero , Tucumán and Catamarca. Salta stands out for its geographic and climatic heterogeneity, from the desert coldness of the Andes and the Puna to the subtropical heat of the jungle, with cool fertile valleys, mountains and rivers in between.

Salta is the gateway to the Andes of Argentina and it is definitely a city with different cultural traits from the rest of the country with more indigenous people, music and arts that are more synonymous to the Andean region of South America, as commonly found in Bolivia and Peru.

en.h1: End of the World and Beagle Channel: what to see in Ushuaia
en.title: Ushuaia Travel Guide | What to See, Best Places & Tips
content_excerpts: Ushuaia, nestled in the heart of Patagonia, Argentina, stirs the imagination of countless adventurers across the globe. This legendary locale invites travelers to witness the raw movements of Mother Earth herself. Situated at the southernmost reaches of the Patagonian plains, in the remote Tierra del Fuego Province and the Islas del Atlántico Sur, the majestic Andes mountains dominate the landscape. Their towering peaks frame glacial valleys, pristine peat bogs, and ancient forests, creating an awe-inspiring paradise at the edge of the world.

Belize City is the largest city in the Central American country of Belize and was once the capital of the former British Honduras.

Embark on an unforgettable journey with guided tours of Belize City, a vibrant destination known for its rich heritage and spectacular landscapes. Explore the city's culinary delights and immerse yourself in its unique culture as you discover why it’s a top tourist destination.

As a busy port city, Belize City is the commercial center of the country. The largest hotels are found here, with conference facilities and professional services, as well as restaurants, bars, nightlife, Belize’s only cruise passenger terminal, the Museum of Belize and numerous historical sites. Quick connections—either by short flight or water taxi—to offshore islands make for great day tours of snorkeling, diving and relaxing.

Located one mile west of Belize Barrier Reef, Caye Caulker is a four mile long island, part of a chain of islands forming the Belize Barrier Reef. Caye Caulker has a relaxing atmosphere with white sand streets, golf carts for transportation, and casual dress with no shoes. The weather is usually quite pleasant year around. You can enjoy sailing, diving, birding, jungle tours, fishing, and windsurfing in the clear azure waters of the Caribbean.
